findings.text: Provides invalidation of cached block device aliases over a logical interval. It converts the starting block and length into a folio index range using the device block size, walks resident folios that carry buffers, and for each buffer whose mapped block lies inside the interval it drops dirty state, waits for ongoing I/O and drops request state. Folios without buffers are skipped, locking is per folio, and the walk yields the processor between batches and stops at end of range.

Requires the caller to hold the folio locked on entry and returns the existing buffer ring when present, otherwise creates one sized from the inode block size with a caller supplied initial state. The helper asserts the locked precondition and does not perform mapping or I/O itself.

Describes full folio writeback for block mapped files. It ensures buffers exist with dirty and uptodate initial state, computes first and last file blocks from folio position and inode size, cleans buffers beyond end of file, maps dirty unmapped or delayed buffers through a filesystem callback, clears delay and new states and invalidates device aliases for fresh blocks. It then locks buffers, moves dirty state to async write state, starts folio writeback, submits each async buffer for write with completion handling, unlocks the folio, and on mapping failure submits already mapped buffers, records the error on the mapping and still completes writeback accounting.
Single block convenience wrapper that invalidates device aliases for the device and block number recorded in a given buffer. It delegates to the range invalidator with length one.

Zeroes portions of newly allocated blocks inside a locked folio. It requires the folio locked, does nothing when no buffers are attached, and for each buffer still marked new that overlaps the caller range it zeroes the intersection when the folio as a whole is not uptodate, marks that buffer uptodate, then clears new and marks dirty. Buffers outside the range keep their state.

Translates a filesystem extent description into buffer state for one file block. It rejects mappings that end before the requested offset, treats holes as new when the buffer is not uptodate or beyond end of file, treats delayed allocation as mapped plus delayed plus uptodate with conditional new, treats unwritten as new plus unwritten before falling into mapped handling, and for mapped extents computes the device block number from extent address and offset, marks mapped, marks new on fresh or beyond size extents, and rejects unexpected types or racing block device truncation.

Prepares a locked folio for a byte range write. It creates buffers if missing, derives block size and first file block, then visits each block. Blocks outside the target inherit uptodate when the folio is uptodate. Inside the target it clears stale new state, maps unmapped buffers through either a filesystem callback or extent translation, invalidates aliases for fresh blocks, zeroes partially covered fresh blocks at the edges, issues nonblocking reads for non uptodate blocks that straddle the range boundaries, waits for those reads, and on any failure zeroes newly allocated portions before returning an error.
Starts a buffer read only when the buffer is neither uptodate nor already locked, passing through caller I/O flags. It is a conditional nonblocking read starter with no wait.
Thin wrapper that begins a folio write using only a filesystem block mapping callback, with no extent description. It forwards folio, position, length and callback to the combined begin routine.

Finalizes a folio range after data copy. Buffers fully outside the committed interval that lack uptodate prevent folio wide uptodate promotion, buffers inside gain uptodate and dirty, new markings are cleared everywhere visited, the scan can stop early when the folio started uptodate and the end is reached, and the folio is promoted to uptodate only when no visited outside buffer remained non uptodate.

Entry for buffered writes that locates or creates a locked folio for the target position with write intent, invokes the combined begin routine for mapping and preparation, and on failure unlocks and releases the folio and returns a null folio with an error. On success it returns the locked prepared folio through an out parameter.

Completes a copied range with short write handling. When fewer bytes were copied than requested and the folio was not already uptodate the operation is reduced to zero length to avoid exposing torn partial buffers, newly allocated tails between copied and requested ends are zeroed, cache flushing is performed, and only the actually copied prefix is committed.

Generic buffered write completion that first commits through the block layer, extends inode size while still holding the folio lock when the write passes current size, then unlocks and releases the folio, notifies about a gap when the write started beyond old size, and marks the inode dirty after folio unlock to shorten lock hold and preserve journal ordering.

Defines size store ordering by configuration. On narrow word multiprocessor builds it disables preemption around a sequence count protected store, on narrow word preemptible builds it disables preemption around a plain store, and otherwise it uses release ordering so that prior content updates become visible before the size change observed with acquire ordering.

Reports whether every buffer overlapping a folio byte interval is uptodate. It returns false when no buffers exist, clamps the query to folio bounds, rejects queries touching both first and last blocks as not partial, and otherwise scans the ring for the interval and returns false on the first non uptodate overlap.

Entry for reading a whole folio through block mapping. It creates buffers, computes first and last blocks from folio position and size limit with special handling for verity inodes, zeroes and marks uptodate unmapped blocks beyond or without backing, skips already uptodate buffers, locks others, chains asynchronous reads submitting each predecessor while holding the next, marks the folio mapped to disk when no mapping work was needed, submits the final pending read or completes the folio synchronously when nothing was submitted, and records mapping errors as folio read failure without failing the call itself.

Expands a contiguous file to a larger size by validating the new size then performing a zero length write at the target offset through address space operations, expecting no bytes to be reported as written.

Fills the gap between current committed length and a write position with zeroes using filesystem write operations. It walks whole intermediate folios and a final partial folio, aligns extended length up to block size when the start is unaligned, throttles dirty pages after each folio, aborts on pending fatal signals, and propagates begin or end errors while asserting that successful ends report full length.

Contiguous write entry that first zero fills any gap up to the write position, aligns the committed length to block size when the write extends beyond it from an unaligned start, then delegates to the standard block begin path for folio acquisition and preparation.

Fault handler for writable mappings that locks the faulted folio, validates that it still belongs to the inode mapping and lies within size with truncation reported as fault, clamps length to end of file, prepares the range through the combined begin routine, commits the whole clamped range, marks the folio dirty and waits for stability. Early validation or preparation failures unlock and return an error.

Establishes a two level locking discipline. Folio lock serializes buffer creation, begin preparation, commit and read setup and pins buffer heads against reclaim, while individual buffer locks serialize state changes and I/O submission. Range invalidation uses folio lock rather than a global mapping spinlock because sleeping is allowed and scales better. Nonblocking writeback uses trylock and redirties the folio on contention instead of waiting, and synchronous paths wait on buffers for read completion or prior write completion.

Describes buffers as a circular list anchored from a folio, linked through a per page next field and reachable from folio helpers. Each element carries a device pointer, device block number, size, and state flags for mapped, new, dirty, uptodate, delay, unwritten, request and async read or write. Size is uniform within a folio and derived from inode block bits, and the ring is empty until creation.

Identifies races handled without full exclusion. Buffers outside size may be dirtied concurrently and are cleaned rather than written, dirty state appearing after inspection leaves the folio dirty for a later pass, block device size checks can race truncation and are treated as I/O errors, nonblocking writeback may repeatedly redirty under contention with throttling left to higher layers, and async read completion relies on absence of async state to avoid mistaking a synchronously locked buffer for pending I/O.

Requires that newly mapped blocks invalidate stale device page cache aliases before use. Mapping paths for write, begin and fresh extent translation invoke single block alias invalidation when new state is observed, ensuring later device reads do not see old contents.
